title: The Packaging Complaint
brief: A retail customer of Meridian Foods reports that cartons from production batch {{b}} are splitting at the base during transport: 46 of 600 cartons in one delivery. They ask for a response within 2 working days. You have 12 visit points to contain, find the cause, and prepare the response.

actions.label: Other deliveries from the same carton lot
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Complaint CP-412 for batch {{b}} was logged the same day with photos and an owner.
Carton lot CT-77 was used for 4 batches including {{b}}; 3 of them have shipped to 2 other customers with no notice or hold.
evidence.whyItMatters: Containment must cover all output made with the suspect input.
evidence.missedExplanation: Trace the input lot to every batch.

evidence.text: Receiving record for carton lot CT-77 shows no board strength check; the specification requires 1 test per lot.
evidence.whyItMatters: Externally provided packaging must be verified against its specification.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check that receiving tests match the specification.

evidence.text: Cartons are stored next to the wash area; the humidity log shows 78 percent on 3 days in week 18.
evidence.whyItMatters: Preservation of materials includes suitable storage conditions; humidity may weaken board.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask about storage conditions for packaging.

evidence.text: Case erector glue settings match the set sheet and are checked each shift.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that narrows the cause.

evidence.text: Line lead: "The cartons felt thinner from the new supplier batch. I mentioned it on the shift report."
Supplier change notice SCN-9 (board grade from 32 ECT to 29 ECT) was received 6 weeks ago and filed; no review or approval recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes in supplied products must be evaluated before acceptance.
evidence.missedExplanation: Follow supplier notices to an approval record.

evidence.text: The carton supplier is approved with a current evaluation.
evidence.whyItMatters: Approval is current; the gap is in reviewing the change.

evidence.text: Complaint procedure requires a response within 2 working days with containment and next steps.
Pallet wrapping uses 5 turns of film, as the instruction states.
Forklift traffic is busy near dispatch.
evidence.whyItMatters: Busy traffic is not linked to base splitting here.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Traffic is not linked to the defect.

evidence.text: Shift report from week 17 notes "thin cartons"; no one followed it up.
evidence.whyItMatters: Information from staff about potential problems should be considered and acted on.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read shift reports from before the complaint.

decisions.prompt: What should the response to the customer include?
options: Containment (all batches packed in carton lot CT-77 held or under review, other customers informed), the cause found so far, the corrective action plan with dates, and a contact
A statement that the product inside is fine
A request that the customer handles cartons more carefully
decisions.rationale: The customer needs to know exposure is limited and the cause is being removed.

containment: Hold remaining stock packed in carton lot CT-77 and notify the other 2 customers
correction: Repack affected stock in conforming cartons as authorized
cause: Supplier change notices are filed without review, receiving tests are skipped, and staff reports are not followed up
corrective: Route supplier notices to technical review, enforce the board test at receiving, and review shift report issues daily
effectiveness: Track carton complaints and receiving test completion for six months

debriefText.found: You traced the input lot across batches and customers.
debriefText.missed: A staff report or supplier notice often warns of a problem before the customer does.
debriefText.falseFinding: Pallet wrapping and forklift traffic were not linked.
